entries.label: Emperor-centred ultranationalism
entries.rationale: During 1931–1945 military influence, imperial expansion and kokutai doctrine centred the emperor and Japanese national polity. The regime was not Nazi Germany; its relationship to the wider category of fascism is debated.

sources.title: Japan: Key points in modern history

ideology.name: Japanese Imperial Ultranationalism
ideology.rationale: Official kokutai and imperial mobilisation establish a distinct emperor-centred doctrine. The reference is scoped to 1937–1945 within the country’s 1931–1945 period, not a claim of one unchanging ideology or equivalence to German Nazism.

entries.label: Oligarchic republicanism
entries.rationale: Merchant regents, provincial institutions and the House of Orange competed within a confederated republic. Neoconservatism is a twentieth-century movement and is anachronistic as the republic’s classification.

Beyond Republicanism: Interest of State in Interest van Holland

ideology.name: Dutch Commercial Republicanism
ideology.rationale: Commercial and regent republican thought is a documented strand of the Dutch Republic. Its 1650–1672 doctrinal scope represents the regent tradition within the wider 1650–1702 period; Orangist competitors and colonial practices are not erased.

entries.label: Napoleonic imperial rule
entries.rationale: Napoleon’s hereditary imperial regime combined personal authority, plebiscitary legitimacy, civil law and revolutionary legacies. Bonapartism describes this political tradition and its later development; fascism emerged more than a century afterward.

sources.title: Was the Napoleonic regime a military dictatorship?
Le Code Civil: naissance, principes et posterite

ideology.name: Bonapartism
ideology.rationale: Early Napoleonic imperial institutions form the foundations of Bonapartism. The name and fuller movement developed after 1815; this comparison is expressly to its early foundations, not Napoleon III’s later programme.

entries.label: Marxism–Leninism
entries.rationale: The SED’s official Marxist–Leninist doctrine and Soviet-aligned party state governed during the Honecker period. Maoism is a distinct Chinese revolutionary tradition and is not the GDR’s state ideology.

ideology.name: Marxism–Leninism
ideology.rationale: The SED governed under Marxism–Leninism during the assessed Honecker period. The broad doctrinal profile differs from specific GDR enforcement and is not Maoism.

entries.label: Titoism and self-management socialism
entries.rationale: Tito’s Yugoslavia combined communist party leadership, social ownership, worker self-management, federal decentralisation and nonalignment. Cuban Socialism is a different national tradition, despite overlapping axis scores.

sources.publisher: Coordinamento Nazionale per la Jugoslavia (Yugoslav primary text)
sources.title: Constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

ideology.name: Titoism
ideology.rationale: Self-management, social ownership, federalism and non-alignment establish the Titoist doctrine. Constitutional ideals and governing enforcement differ; numerical resemblance does not make this Cuban Socialism.

limits: Historical doctrine is selected from evidence, not asserted to be the numerical nearest. The five existing 240-question country records and all other doctrine records are unmodified.
